newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvian PM, SAS meet on Russia air row.
newsitem.headline: Latvian PM, SAS meet on Russia air row.

text.p: Latvian Prime Minister Andris Shkele on Thursday met the vice-president of Scandinavian Airlines, Lars Lindgren, over a row with Russia on flights between Moscow and Riga.
"The vice-president of SAS expressed the wish that this problem should be solved in the near future by financial means," Shkele's office said in a statement but did not elaborate.
It said the SAS official told Shkele the airline intended to resume flights to Russia next year.
Russia has refused to grant rights to Latvia's Air Baltic, in which SAS has a large stake, to fly to Moscow.
It wants Latvia to repays debts for landing fees run up by the previous state-owned Latvian airline, Latavio, which later became Air Baltic.
Latvia recently refused to confirm the winter timetable for Russia's Aeroflot which was then forced to suspend its flights to Latvia.
The route is now operated only by Russia's Transaero and Latvian-based Riair, which has a code-sharing deal with Transaero.
The press office said Shkele told Lindgren he would do all he could to solve the dispute, via financial and political means.
Shkele said an important step would be the visit of Latvian Transport Minister Vilis Krishtopans to Moscow in December.
SAS is also involved in row in Estonia, which may cause the suspension of flights between the Baltic state and Scandinavia from November 16.
